lesson.scenario: Two profile replicas preserve concurrent edits until a causally dominating merge resolves both siblings.

steps.title: Read a shared causal base
steps.narration: Both replicas hold profile P-42 version {east:4,west:7} with phone=111 and city=Paris before connectivity fails.

steps.invariant: A version is discarded only when another vector is greater than or equal in every component and greater in at least one; concurrent vectors remain siblings until a new version causally descends from all of them.

production.scenario: Figma design comments sync between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 when editors reconnect after offline work.
components: global designers submitting offline thread edits from web and iPad clients
service boundary that authenticates file members and terminates sync sessions
control-plane service that applies vector clocks to classify ancestry or concurrency per thread
durable authority in DynamoDB global tables for thread mutations and merged versions
serves merged comment threads back to browsers and mobile clients worldwide
repair path that replays concurrent branches needing product-specific resolution
observability path for concurrency spikes, replay lag, and repair backlog
flows: Mobile editors reconnect and submit buffered comment mutations for one document thread.
The API asks the vector clock service whether the incoming mutation is descendant, ancestor, or concurrent.
The mechanism records the accepted mutation into the authoritative event store with merged metadata.
The fanout tier rebuilds the viewer projection from the durable thread history.
Concurrent branches that need product rules or moderator review are scheduled for repair.
The repair worker replays disputed edits through the same vector clock service after policy inputs arrive.
Operations dashboards track conflict rate, unresolved branches, and repair latency by region.
